nodes.name: Weight decay update
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update
nodes.statement: $\bm{\theta}_{t+1} = (1 - \lambda) \bm{\theta}_t - \alpha \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t),$
assumptions: $\lambda$ defines the rate of the weight decay per step
$\nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_t)$ is the $t$-th batch gradient to be multiplied by a learning rate $\alpha$

nodes.name: Bayesian filtering mean update
nodes.section: 3 Justification of Decoupled Weight Decay via a View of Adaptive Gradient Methods as Bayesian Filtering
nodes.statement: $\bm{\mu}_{post} = \bm{\mu}_{prior} + \bm{\Sigma}_{post} \times \bm{g},$
assumptions: $\bm{g}$ is the gradient of the log likelihood of the mini batch at time $t$

nodes.name: Gaussian state-transition distribution
nodes.section: 3 Justification of Decoupled Weight Decay via a View of Adaptive Gradient Methods as Bayesian Filtering
nodes.statement: $P(\bm{\theta}_{t+1} \mid \bm{\theta}_t) = \mathcal{N}((\bm{I}-\bm{A}) \bm{\theta}_t, \bm{Q}),$
assumptions: $\bm{Q}$ is the covariance of Gaussian perturbations of the weights
$\bm{A}$ is a regularizer to avoid values growing unboundedly over time

nodes.name: Normalized weight decay
nodes.section: Appendix B.1 Normalized Weight Decay
nodes.statement: $\lambda = \lambda_{norm} \sqrt{ \frac{b}{B T} }$
assumptions: $b$ is the batch size
$B$ is the total number of training points
$T$ is the total number of epochs

nodes.name: Cosine annealing schedule
nodes.section: Appendix B.2 Adam with Cosine Annealing and Warm Restarts
assumptions: $\eta^{(i)}_{min}$ and $\eta^{(i)}_{max}$ are ranges for the multiplier
$T_{cur}$ accounts for how many epochs have been performed since the last restart

nodes.name: Simplified cosine annealing schedule
nodes.section: Appendix B.2 Adam with Cosine Annealing and Warm Restarts
assumptions: For $\eta^{(i)}_{max}=1$ and $\eta^{(i)}_{min}=0$

nodes.name: Weight decay = L$_2$ reg for standard SGD
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update
nodes.statement: Standard SGD with base learning rate $\alpha$ executes the same steps on batch loss functions $f_t(\bm{\theta})$ with weight decay $\lambda$ (defined in Equation \ref{eq:wdecay}) as it executes without weight decay on $f_{t}^{\text{reg}}(\bm{\theta}) = f_t(\bm{\theta}) + \frac{\lambda'}{2} \norm{\bm{\theta}}_2^2$, with $\lambda' = \frac{\lambda}{\alpha}$.
assumptions: Standard SGD with base learning rate $\alpha$
with weight decay $\lambda$ (defined in Equation \ref{eq:wdecay})
$f_{t}^{\text{reg}}(\bm{\theta}) = f_t(\bm{\theta}) + \frac{\lambda'}{2} \norm{\bm{\theta}}_2^2$, with $\lambda' = \frac{\lambda}{\alpha}$
conclusions: executes the same steps on batch loss functions $f_t(\bm{\theta})$ with weight decay $\lambda$ ... as it executes without weight decay on $f_{t}^{\text{reg}}(\bm{\theta})$

nodes.name: Weight decay = scale-adjusted $L_2$ reg for adaptive gradient algorithm with fixed preconditioner
nodes.section: 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-based Update
nodes.statement: Let $O$ denote an algorithm with the same characteristics as in Proposition 2, and using a fixed preconditioner matrix $\textbf{M}_t = \text{diag}(\vc{s})^{-1}$ (with $s_i>0$ for all $i$). Then, $O$ with base learning rate $\alpha$ executes the same steps on batch loss functions $f_t(\bm{\theta})$ with weight decay $\lambda$ as it executes without weight decay on the scale-adjusted regularized batch loss \begin{equation}f_{t}^{\text{sreg}}(\bm{\theta}) = f_t(\bm{\theta}) + \frac{\lambda'}{2\alpha} \norm{\bm{\theta} \odot{} \sqrt{\vc{s}}}_2^2,\end{equation} where $\odot$ and $\sqrt{\cdot}$ denote element-wise multiplication and square root, respectively, and $\lambda' = \frac{\lambda}{\alpha}$.

using a fixed preconditioner matrix $\textbf{M}_t = \text{diag}(\vc{s})^{-1}$ (with $s_i>0$ for all $i$)

nodes.statement: \STATE{\textbf{given} initial learning rate $\alpha \in \R$, momentum factor $\beta_1 \in \R$, weight decay/L$_2$ regularization factor $\lambda \in \R$} \STATE{\textbf{initialize} time step $t \leftarrow 0$, parameter vector $\bm{\theta}_{t=0} \in \R^n$, first moment vector $\vc{m}_{t=0} \leftarrow \vc{0}$, schedule multiplier $\eta_{t=0} \in \R$} \REPEAT \STATE{$t \leftarrow t + 1$} \STATE{$\nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_{t-1}) \leftarrow \text{SelectBatch}(\bm{\theta}_{t-1})$} \COMMENT{select batch and return the corresponding gradient} \STATE{$\vc{g}_t \leftarrow \nabla f_t(\bm{\theta}_{t-1})$ \adam{+ \lambda\bm{\theta}_{t-1}}} \STATE{$\eta_t \leftarrow \text{SetScheduleMultiplier}(t)$} \COMMENT{can be fixed, decay, be used for warm restarts} \STATE{$\vc{m}_t \leftarrow \beta_1 \vc{m}_{t-1} + \eta_t \alpha \vc{g}_t $} \STATE{$\bm{\theta}_t \leftarrow \bm{\theta}_{t-1} - \vc{m}_t$ \ouradam{- \eta_t \lambda\bm{\theta}_{t-1}}} \UNTIL{ \textit{stopping criterion is met} } \RETURN{optimized parameters $\bm{\theta}_t$}

nodes.name: AdamWR
nodes.section: Appendix B.2 Adam with Cosine Annealing and Warm Restarts
nodes.statement: Our proposed \textbf{AdamWR} algorithm represents AdamW (see Algorithm 2) with $\eta_t$ following Eq.\ (\ref{eq:t2}) and $\lambda$ computed at each iteration using normalized weight decay described in Section \ref{sec:normw}.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.section: Appendix A Formal Analysis of Weight Decay vs L$_2$ Regularization
nodes.statement:
The proof for this well-known fact is straight-forward. SGD without weight decay has the following iterates on $f_{t}^{	ext{reg}}( m{	heta}) = f_t( m{	heta}) +  rac{\lambda'}{2} 
orm{ m{	heta}}_2^2$:  egin{equation}  m{	heta}_{t+1} \leftarrow  m{	heta}_t - \alpha 
abla f_{t}^{	ext{reg}}( m{	heta}_t) =  m{	heta}_t - \alpha 
abla f_t( m{	heta}_t) - \alpha \lambda'  m{	heta}_t. \end{equation} SGD with weight decay has the following iterates on $f_t( m{	heta})$:  egin{equation}  m{	heta}_{t+1} \leftarrow (1 - \lambda)  m{	heta}_t - \alpha 
abla f_t( m{	heta}_t). \end{equation} These iterates are identical since $\lambda' =  rac{\lambda}{\alpha}$. \qed

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2
nodes.section: Appendix A Formal Analysis of Weight Decay vs L$_2$ Regularization
nodes.statement:
Similarly to the proof of Proposition 1, the iterates of $O$ without weight decay on $f^{	ext{reg}}_t( m{	heta}) = f_t( m{	heta}) +  rac{1}{2} \lambda' 
orm{ m{	heta}}_2^2$ and $O$ with weight decay $\lambda$ on $f_t$ are, respectively:  egin{eqnarray}  m{	heta}_{t+1} &\leftarrow&  m{	heta}_t - \alpha \lambda' \mathbf{M}_t  m{	heta}_t - \alpha \mathbf{M}_t 
abla f_t( m{	heta}_t).\  m{	heta}_{t+1} &\leftarrow& (1 - \lambda)  m{	heta}_t - \alpha \mathbf{M}_t 
abla f_t( m{	heta}_t). \end{eqnarray} The equality of these iterates for all $ m{	heta}_t$ would imply $\lambda m{	heta}_t = \alpha \lambda' \mathbf{M}_t m{	heta}_t$. This can only hold for all $ m{	heta}_t$ if $\mathbf{M}_t = k \mathbf{I}$, with $k\in\mathbb{R}$, which is not the case for $O$. Therefore, no L$_2$ regularizer $\lambda' 
orm{ m{	heta}}_2^2$ exists that makes the iterates equivalent. \qed

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3
nodes.section: Appendix A Formal Analysis of Weight Decay vs L$_2$ Regularization
nodes.statement:
$O$ without weight decay has the following iterates on $f_{t}^{	ext{sreg}}( m{	heta}) = f_t( m{	heta}) +  rac{\lambda'}{2} 
orm{ m{	heta} \odot{} \sqrt{\vc{s}}}_2^2$:  egin{eqnarray}  m{	heta}_{t+1} & \leftarrow & m{	heta}_t - \alpha 
abla f_{t}^{	ext{sreg}}( m{	heta}_t)/\vc{s}\ &=&  m{	heta}_t - \alpha 
abla f_t( m{	heta}_t)/\vc{s} - \alpha \lambda'  m{	heta}_t \odot \vc{s} / \vc{s}\ &=&  m{	heta}_t - \alpha 
abla f_t( m{	heta}_t)/\vc{s} - \alpha \lambda'  m{	heta}_t, \end{eqnarray} where the division by $\vc{s}$ is element-wise. $O$ with weight decay has the following iterates on $f_t( m{	heta})$:  egin{eqnarray}  m{	heta}_{t+1} &\leftarrow& (1 - \lambda)  m{	heta}_t - \alpha 
abla f( m{	heta}_t) / \vc{s}\ &=&  m{	heta}_t - \alpha 
abla f( m{	heta}_t) / \vc{s} -\lambda  m{	heta}_t , \end{eqnarray} These iterates are identical since $\lambda' =  rac{\lambda}{\alpha}$. \qed
